The '''WTA 1000 tournaments''' are a category of [[tennis]] tournaments on the [[WTA Tour]], governed by the [[Women's Tennis Association]]. The old [[WTA Premier tournaments|WTA Premier Mandatory and Premier 5]] tournaments merged into a single highest tier implemented in the 2021 schedule reorganization. Only four of the nine WTA 1000 tournaments were mandatory until 2024, when the category expanded to ten mandatory tournaments.

The ranking points awarded to the winners of these tournaments are 1,000. This compares to 2,000 points for winning a [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] tournament ("major"), up to 1,500 points for winning the [[WTA Finals]], 500 points for winning a [[WTA 500 tournament]], and 250 for winning a [[WTA 250 tournament]].

== History ==
Following the unification of the two women's tennis circuits that were managed within the WTA Tour in [[1987 Virginia Slims World Championship Series|1987]] — the [[Virginia Slims Circuit]] and the [[ILTF Women's International Grand Prix Circuit]] — WTA 1000 tournaments were known as WTA Category 5 and WTA Category 6.<ref>{{cite web |date=1988 |title=Rules and Regulations |url=https://www.industrydocumentslibrary.ucsf.edu/tobacco/docs/yrlb0017 |publisher=[[Women's Tennis Association]] (WITA) |via=[[University of California San Francisco]] (UCSF)'s [[Truth Tobacco Industry Documents]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Barrett |first1=John |url=https://archive.org/details/worldoftennis1990000unse |title=World of Tennis 1990 |date=1990 |publisher=Willow Books |isbn=0-00-218355-2 |location=Great Britain |page=163}}</ref> Later renamed WTA Tier I tournaments in [[1990 WTA Tour|1990]], results in these tournaments would give players more points than almost every other tournament excluding Grand Slams and the year-end championships.

Prior to [[2009 WTA Tour|2009]], the WTA released a "Roadmap" outlining changes made to the tour in an effort to streamline the tour calendar.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rhoden |first=William C. |date=2 September 2008 |title=WTA Tour Road Map to Bring Direction |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/09/03/sports/tennis/03rhoden.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126021012/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/09/03/sports/tennis/03rhoden.html |archive-date=26 November 2022 |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=New York Times}}</ref> With this reform came the abolishment of the tier system, replaced by WTA Premier and WTA International categories. Pre-existing Tier I tournaments were split into two categories: Premier Mandatory, which required all top 10 players to attend, and Premier 5, which required at least seven top 10 players.<ref>{{cite news |last=Tandon |first=Kamakshi |date=29 October 2008 |title=Ten notable features of the Roadmap |url=https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/columns/story?columnist=kamakshi_tandon&id=3670301 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805173255/https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/columns/story?columnist=kamakshi_tandon&id=3670301 |archive-date=5 August 2021 |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=ESPN}}</ref>

At the beginning of the [[2021 WTA Tour|2021 season]], the WTA announced they would once again revamp their tournament categorisation system to one reminiscent of the ATP Tour, in an effort to "create consistency between professional tennis".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2020 |title=WTA unveils comprehensive rebrand |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1922290/wta-unveils-comprehensive-rebrand |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210106170517/https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1922290/wta-unveils-comprehensive-rebrand |archive-date=6 January 2021 |access-date=1 October 2025 |website=WTA Tour |publisher=Women's Tennis Association (WTA)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2020 |title=WTA will align tournament categories with ATP from 2021 season |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/12148935/wta-will-align-tournament-categories-with-atp-from-2021-season |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220926131953/https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/12148935/wta-will-align-tournament-categories-with-atp-from-2021-season |archive-date=26 September 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> This revamp once again combined the Premier Mandatory and Premier 5 categories, though WTA 1000 tournaments were still split into mandatory and non-mandatory events, with less ranking points given to the latter.<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 WTA Rulebook |url=https://photoresources.wtatennis.com/wta/document/2021/03/08/d6d2c650-e3b4-42e7-ab2b-e539d4586033/2021Rulebook.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519054739/https://photoresources.wtatennis.com/wta/document/2021/03/08/d6d2c650-e3b4-42e7-ab2b-e539d4586033/2021Rulebook.pdf |archive-date=19 May 2022 |access-date=1 October 2025 |publisher=Women's Tennis Association |page=148}}</ref> This was until 2024, when the WTA announced that all WTA 1000 tournaments would be mandatory.<ref name="2024points">{{Cite web |title=WTA ranking point chart |url=https://www.itftennis.com/media/11225/2024-ranking-points.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204053634/https://www.itftennis.com/media/11225/2024-ranking-points.pdf |archive-date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=21 June 2024 |website=itftennis.com}}</ref>

=== Historic names ===
* 1990–2008: WTA Tier I
* 2009–2020: WTA Premier Mandatory / Premier 5
* 2021–present: WTA 1000

== Tournaments ==
As of 2025, there are ten tournaments that are part of the WTA 1000.<ref>{{cite web |title=2025 WTA Calendar |url=https://wtafiles.wtatennis.com/pdf/calendar/calendar.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805064239/https://wtafiles.wtatennis.com/pdf/calendar/calendar.pdf |archive-date=5 August 2025 |access-date=1 October 2025 |publisher=Women's Tennis Association}}</ref> Eight of these tournaments are held on outdoor hardcourts whilst the other two are held on clay. Additionally, there are three tournaments that are considered WTA only: the [[WTA Qatar Open|Qatar Open]], [[Dubai Tennis Championships]] and [[Wuhan Open]].

When the WTA 1000 category was originally established, there were four mandatory tournaments ([[Indian Wells Open|Indian Wells]], [[Miami Open (tennis)|Miami]], [[Madrid Open (tennis)|Madrid]] and [[China Open (tennis)|Beijing]]) and five non-mandatory tournaments (Dubai, [[Italian Open (tennis)|Rome]], [[Canadian Open (tennis)|Canada]], [[Cincinnati Open|Cincinnati]] and [[Wuhan Open|Wuhan]]), though Beijing and Wuhan were both cancelled that year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myles |first=Stephanie |date=2021-07-01 |title=WTA officially cancels 2021 fall Asian swing |url=http://opencourt.ca/2021/07/01/wta-officially-cancels-2021-fall-asian-swing/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220924165036/https://opencourt.ca/2021/07/01/wta-officially-cancels-2021-fall-asian-swing/ |archive-date=2022-09-24 |access-date=12 August 2025 |website=Open Court |language=en-US}}</ref> Wuhan Open was temporarily replaced by the [[Guadalajara Open Akron|Guadalajara Open]] in 2022, following the cancellation of the two Chinese tournaments for the second year in a row,<ref>{{cite news |last=Myles |first=Stephanie |date=10 May 2022 |title=WTA to add 1000 event in Guadalajara in October |url=https://opencourt.ca/2022/05/10/report-wta-to-add-1000-event-in-guadalajara-in-october |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251001170204/https://opencourt.ca/2022/05/10/report-wta-to-add-1000-event-in-guadalajara-in-october/ |archive-date=1 October 2025 |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=Open Court}}</ref> though Beijing returned the following year.

The 2024 season saw all WTA 1000 tournaments become mandatory.<ref name="2024points" /> Wuhan returned whilst Guadalajara was demoted to a WTA 500 tournament. Doha and Dubai, which had been alternating between WTA 1000 and WTA 500 status every year since 2015, both became permanent WTA 1000 tournaments.
